monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and intensity compared to last month, with significantly reduced running frequency and distance, though aerobic efficiency remains stable and cadence is slightly lower.
monthly_review.highlight: The runner completed only 2 runs this month versus 9 last month — a 78% reduction in session frequency — despite having 27 days remaining.

goal_tracker.message: You need 30.6 more km across 7 sessions in the remaining 27 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~4.4 km per session.

insights.title: Stable efficiency despite pace variability
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency held steady at 13.62 (May) vs 13.66 (April), even as average pace slowed by +35 sec/km — suggesting maintained neuromuscular coordination under reduced load.

insights.title: Drastic shift toward low-intensity effort
insights.body: Zone 1 effort rose from 23% to 50% of total time, while Zone 3–5 dropped from 45% to 17%, indicating a pronounced de-load or unintended under-training this month.

insights.title: Cadence and stride length diverged under slower pacing
insights.body: On the May 5 run (10:07 min/km, HR 121 bpm), cadence was high (144 spm) but stride length collapsed to 68.3 m — 20% shorter than the April 29 run (7.77 min/km, 88.7 m), signaling inefficient form at very easy paces.

insights.title: Low ground contact time persists despite reduced load
insights.body: Average ground contact time remained consistently low (301–327 ms across recent runs), matching elite recreational norms — suggesting strong leg stiffness and recovery readiness, even with minimal recent volume.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run at HR ≤138 bpm on your next run, using the April 28 pace (8:44 min/km) as a target to rebuild aerobic TE without overexertion.
recommendations.reason: Your April 28 run achieved 2.5 aerobic TE at 132 bpm and 148 spm — replicating that intensity will help restore training stimulus without triggering fatigue.

recommendations.action: Add one 20-min Zone 3 interval session: 4 x 3-min @ HR 150–158 bpm with 90-sec walk recovery, keeping cadence ≥144 spm throughout.
recommendations.reason: Zone 3 contribution fell to 16% this month (vs 26% last month), and your best recent pace (428 sec/km on Apr 29) occurred during Zone 3 effort — rebuilding this zone supports pace resilience.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km form-focused run at 9:30–10:00 min/km, consciously maintaining stride length ≥78 m (measured via Garmin) and cadence ≥140 spm — use May 5’s data (68.3 m, 144 spm) as a baseline to improve.
recommendations.reason: Stride length dropped sharply at slow paces (68.3 m on May 5 vs 85.2–88.7 m on faster runs), indicating gait breakdown that limits efficiency gains.

weekly_focus.description: Focus on restoring consistent Zone 2 volume and reintroducing controlled Zone 3 efforts to re-anchor pace–HR relationships, while reinforcing stride-length discipline at all paces.
suggested_sessions: 3 km form-aware easy run (focus: stride length ≥78 m, cadence ≥140 spm)
